title: Smart city
desc: Coordinated traffic lights, street lights & a parking sensor on one build
content_html:
Overview

The Smart City build brings three city subsystems onto one Arduino: a traffic-light intersection, an automatic street light that turns on when it gets dark, and a smart-parking bay that senses whether a car is present and shows the status on an LCD. It is the flagship "Solve" project — students integrate several sensors and outputs into one working model of their town.

Materials

  • Arduino Uno & USB cable — 1 (Nerokas, nerokas.co.ke)
  • Breadboard & jumper wires — 1 set (Nerokas / Pixel Electronics, pixelelectronics.co.ke)
  • LEDs: red, yellow, green for traffic + 1 for street light + 2 for parking status — 6 total, with 220Ω resistors
  • LDR (light-dependent resistor) + 10kΩ resistor — 1 (voltage divider into A0)
  • HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor — 1 (parking)
  • 16x2 LCD (parallel / HD44780) + 10kΩ potentiometer for contrast — 1

Optional for extensions: DHT11, MQ135 air-quality, PIR motion, soil-moisture, servo, buzzer, relay, ESP8266/ESP32 for IoT.

How It Works

  • Traffic lights cycle green → yellow → red on a timer written as a non-blocking state machine (using millis()), so the rest of the city keeps running.
  • Street light reads the LDR each loop; when the reading drops below the "dark" threshold the LED switches on — just like real dusk-to-dawn lighting.
  • Smart parking pings the ultrasonic sensor: a car within 10 cm marks the bay occupied (red LED), otherwise free (green LED), and the LCD shows FREE / FULL.

Step-by-Step Build

  1. Build the traffic light first (3 LEDs + resistors) and get the timed sequence running.
  2. Add the LDR as a voltage divider into A0; add the street-light LED and test dark/light.
  3. Wire the HC-SR04 (TRIG 9, ECHO 8) and the two parking LEDs; test the distance reading on the Serial Monitor.
  4. Wire the LCD (contrast pot to the middle pin) and show the parking status on the bottom row.
  5. Upload the full sketch below and tune DARK and PARK_CM for your room.

Full Code

#include 

// 16x2 LCD in 4-bit mode: rs, en, d4, d5, d6, d7
LiquidCrystal lcd(2, 3, 4, 5, A1, A2);

// --- Pin map ---
const int RED = 13, YEL = 12, GRN = 11;   // traffic light
const int STREET = 10;                    // smart street light LED
const int TRIG = 9, ECHO = 8;             // parking ultrasonic (HC-SR04)
const int P_FREE = 7, P_OCC = 6;          // parking status LEDs
const int LDR = A0;                       // light sensor (analog)

// --- Tuning ---
const unsigned long GREEN_MS = 5000, YELLOW_MS = 2000, RED_MS = 5000;
const int DARK = 400;      // LDR reading below this = "night" (tune on the day)
const int PARK_CM = 10;    // car within 10 cm = bay occupied

int phase = 0;                 // 0 = green, 1 = yellow, 2 = red
unsigned long phaseStart = 0;
unsigned long lastSense = 0;

void setup() {
  int outs[] = {RED, YEL, GRN, STREET, P_FREE, P_OCC};
  for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) pinMode(outs[i], OUTPUT);
  pinMode(TRIG, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(ECHO, INPUT);
  lcd.begin(16, 2);
  lcd.print("Smart City");
  phaseStart = millis();
}

// Read distance in cm; returns -1 on timeout (nothing in range).
long readCm() {
  digitalWrite(TRIG, LOW);  delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(TRIG, HIGH); delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(TRIG, LOW);
  long us = pulseIn(ECHO, HIGH, 30000);   // 30 ms timeout
  return us == 0 ? -1 : us / 58;          // ~58 us per cm (round trip)
}

// Non-blocking traffic light so parking + lights keep updating.
void updateTraffic() {
  unsigned long now = millis();
  unsigned long dur = (phase == 0) ? GREEN_MS : (phase == 1) ? YELLOW_MS : RED_MS;
  if (now - phaseStart >= dur) { phase = (phase + 1) % 3; phaseStart = now; }
  digitalWrite(GRN, phase == 0);
  digitalWrite(YEL, phase == 1);
  digitalWrite(RED, phase == 2);
}

void loop() {
  updateTraffic();

  // Smart street light: switch on automatically when it gets dark.
  digitalWrite(STREET, analogRead(LDR) < DARK ? HIGH : LOW);

  // Smart parking: check the bay twice a second.
  if (millis() - lastSense >= 500) {
    lastSense = millis();
    long cm = readCm();
    bool occupied = (cm > 0 && cm <= PARK_CM);
    digitalWrite(P_OCC, occupied);
    digitalWrite(P_FREE, !occupied);
    lcd.setCursor(0, 1);
    lcd.print(occupied ? "Parking: FULL " : "Parking: FREE ");
  }
}

Common Mistakes & Fixes

SymptomLikely causeFix
Everything freezes during the red lightUsing delay() for the traffic lightUse the millis() state machine shown here so sensors keep reading
Street light never turns on/offDARK threshold wrong for the roomPrint analogRead(LDR) to Serial and set DARK between the light and dark values
Parking always reads FULL or FREEECHO/TRIG swapped, or timeoutCheck wiring; readCm() returns -1 on timeout — treat as "free"
LCD shows blocks or nothingContrast pot not set / miswiredTurn the 10k pot until text appears; recheck rs/en/d4–d7

Discussion Questions

  1. Why is a non-blocking (millis()) traffic light better than one built with delay()?
  2. What real problem in your town could each subsystem help with?
  3. How could the parking bay count several spaces instead of one?
  4. Where would you add a sensor to make the city safer or greener?
  5. What are the trade-offs of automating street lights (cost, safety, energy)?

Extension Challenges

  • Easy: add a second intersection direction; count multiple free parking bays on the LCD.
  • Medium: add an air-quality monitor (MQ135), a weather station (DHT11), automatic pedestrian lighting (PIR), or a home-security intruder alarm (PIR + buzzer).
  • Hard: make the traffic lights respond to traffic volume (ultrasonic), add smart irrigation (soil-moisture + relay), or connect to the internet with an ESP8266/ESP32 and plot temperature, traffic and air quality on an Arduino Cloud / Blynk / ThingSpeak dashboard.
  • Capstone: teams combine subsystems into one miniature city — traffic, smart homes, street lights, parking, environment sensors, an emergency system and an IoT dashboard.
